nodes.label: Ascon C DLL backend lookup order
nodes.rationale: Bundled DLL in native/ascon/bin makes clone-and-run work without manual build; falls back to native/ascon/ascon-c/build then pure-Python ascon library.

nodes.label: Benchmark procedure: 5 warm-up + 50 iterations
nodes.rationale: Use time.perf_counter rather than time.time for higher resolution; discard warm-up runs before recording.

nodes.label: Initial hypothesis: Ascon wins on small files, AES-GCM on large
nodes.rationale: AES-GCM expected to be more competitive on large files thanks to AES-NI hardware acceleration on desktop x86.
nodes.norm_label: initial hypothesis: ascon wins on small files, aes-gcm on large

nodes.rationale: Upload as an additional mode so the existing benchmark pipeline and CSV-only dashboard are not disrupted; makes the presentation demo more convincing.

nodes.label: NIST SP 800-232 Ascon standard
nodes.rationale: Standard changes vs the Ascon submission: little-endian instead of big-endian, updated initial values.

nodes.label: Ascon C implementations (ref, opt64, opt32, bi32, armv7m, avr...)
nodes.rationale: The ref implementation is recommended as the starting point: self-contained, portable, very fast.

nodes.label: Plan A: Benchmark Core
nodes.rationale: Makes AES-GCM vs Ascon results trustworthy and answers the proposal's efficiency-threshold question via official test vectors, statistics, size sweep and environment info.

nodes.label: A Task 1: Official test-vector (KAT) tests
nodes.rationale: Validates the C DLL against 1089 official Ascon-AEAD128 vectors and NIST AES-GCM vectors; skipped if backend is not C.

nodes.label: Latency crossover point (log-log interpolation)
nodes.rationale: Answers the proposal's efficiency-threshold question: size where Ascon/AES latency ratio crosses 1.0. A None result is a valid finding, not a bug.

nodes.label: AES-NI speedup measurement (use_aesni False vs True)
nodes.norm_label: aes-ni speedup measurement (use_aesni false vs true)

nodes.label: Ascon variant caveat: AEAD128 (SP 800-232) vs Ascon-128 v1.2
nodes.rationale: The C DLL implements Ascon-AEAD128 while the Python ascon library Ascon-128 v1.2 is incompatible; Backend column and environment.json record which was used.
nodes.norm_label: ascon variant caveat: aead128 (sp 800-232) vs ascon-128 v1.2

nodes.label: Underscore-prefixed private sample keys convention
nodes.rationale: Raw latency samples ride on result rows via _-prefixed keys, dropped from the main CSV and written to raw_samples.csv, keeping legacy columns intact.

nodes.label: Legacy CSV columns must not be removed
nodes.rationale: EXPECTED_COLUMNS in dashboard_app.py depend on existing CSV columns; new statistics are additive.
nodes.norm_label: legacy csv columns must not be removed

nodes.label: Plan B: Interactive Dashboard Demo
nodes.rationale: Adds presentation-visible demos to the Dash dashboard: tamper, roundtrip hash, nonce reuse, image vs ciphertext, sweep chart and environment panel.

nodes.label: B Task 2: src/demo_tools.py pure demo logic
nodes.norm_label: b task 2: src/demo_tools.py pure demo logic

nodes.label: B Task 4: src/dashboard_analysis.py sweep and environment section
nodes.norm_label: b task 4: src/dashboard_analysis.py sweep and environment section

nodes.label: Nonce reuse demo (AES-GCM leaks all, Ascon first 16 bytes)
nodes.rationale: Verified fact: under nonce reuse AES-GCM leaks the XOR of plaintexts for the full length, while Ascon-AEAD128 leaks only the first block (16 bytes).
nodes.norm_label: nonce reuse demo (aes-gcm leaks all, ascon first 16 bytes)

nodes.label: Pure logic separated from Dash UI modules
nodes.rationale: Logic lives in aead.py and demo_tools.py for testability; dashboard_app.py (960+ lines) is only touched at three small points to avoid bloating it.
nodes.norm_label: pure logic separated from dash ui modules

nodes.label: Component ID prefix convention (demo-, analysis-)
nodes.rationale: New components use distinct prefixes so existing IDs such as upload-data, upload-state and run-benchmark are never changed.

nodes.label: Plan C: Realistic Scenarios
nodes.rationale: Adds API-style small messages, chunked large-file encryption and AES-NI on/off comparison to explain why local results differ from literature.

nodes.label: C Task 1: AES-GCM-noNI variant
nodes.rationale: pycryptodome use_aesni=False emulates devices without AES-NI; AES-GCM 4 MB went from about 5.9 ms to 24.7 ms on the dev machine.

nodes.label: Acceleration scenario (AES-GCM vs noNI vs Ascon)
nodes.norm_label: acceleration scenario (aes-gcm vs noni vs ascon)

nodes.label: Chunk index and last-flag bound into AD
nodes.rationale: AD includes chunk index and final-chunk flag so reordering and truncation of the chunk stream are detected; per-chunk nonce derived from base nonce plus counter avoids key+nonce reuse.
nodes.norm_label: chunk index and last-flag bound into ad

nodes.label: ALGORITHMS unchanged; noNI only via ALL_VARIANTS
nodes.rationale: Plan B demo UI iterates aead.ALGORITHMS, so the noNI variant is exposed only through ALL_VARIANTS to avoid breaking it.
nodes.norm_label: algorithms unchanged; noni only via all_variants

nodes.label: Tests must not assume which algorithm is faster
nodes.rationale: Benchmark results are data; tests check only structure, correctness and overhead, and code must not be tuned to make results look good.
nodes.norm_label: tests must not assume which algorithm is faster
